cards.summary: Generated programs average 4.9% above the updated TypeScript reference. Fifteen of 45 cases are faster; speed is essentially unchanged from the paired Phase 65 compiler.
cards.alt: Generated-program execution history reaches 1.049× the updated TypeScript reference at Phase 66. Separate segments identify timing, interface and reference changes.
cards.caption: The same 45 source/input cases, compared to paired TypeScript runs. P66 uses the updated reference, so it starts a new segment. Historical neighbors are not controlled before/after pairs.
cards.takeaway: All 669 runtime samples pass their output checks. The paired P65 → P66 aggregate changes by +0.038% time: the upstream migration preserves program speed.
cards.cohort: 45 benchmark cases · 23 programs · Phase 66 final07 · direct JavaScript
cards.breakdown_alt: Phase 66 execution ratios grouped into 23 source-program bars; Mandelbrot and raytrace retain the largest gaps to TypeScript.

Five role/case pairs retain drift or spread flags in the source report.

cards.caption: Earlier two-program first-window results remain visible. The current headline measures compilation alone across 23 programs. Separate segments mark the changed clock, workload set and TypeScript reference; the lower current ratio is not one controlled speedup from P58.
cards.takeaway: P61 reduced B2 compilation time by 45.71% in its paired campaign, followed by further reductions at P63–65. The upstream migration preserves those gains: P66 changes by −0.230% against its fresh P65 control, effectively flat.

cards.title: Conformance
cards.summary: The full JavaScript comparison now has zero observed cases where TypeScript passes and Bend fails. Node execution plus exact-module Bun evidence establishes 1,045 distinct passes, versus TypeScript’s 1,044.
cards.alt: Conformance history retains exact frontend comparisons and focused source controls, then adds Phase 66 full JavaScript coverage: 1,045 golden passes, 123 unprintable-main exemptions, one shared failure and one graphics deferral.
cards.caption: Current JS coverage combines 991 fresh Node passes with 54 Bun passes reused after proving identical emitted modules and runtime. Separately, a scoped frontend dependency audit retains 3,174 exact parse/check observations on the updated reference.
cards.takeaway: Of 1,170 eligible fixtures, 123 have unprintable main results, one Process.run fixture fails both compilers and one graphics fixture is deferred. B1 and B2 also pass the focused 96/34/18/2 suites; these overlapping scopes are not added together.

cards.title: Simplicity
cards.summary: The compiler has 23,353 code lines in 115 modules. The upstream migration adds 94 physical lines and 69 code lines over P65 while retaining the compiler’s existing architecture.
cards.alt: Compiler source history through Phase 66 reaches 28,490 physical lines and 23,353 code lines; the latest migration adds 94 physical lines over Phase 65.
cards.caption: Canonical Bend modules only, excluding host code, runtime, tests and generated files. Current code-line counts exclude blanks and whole-line comments; earlier nonblank counts remain separate.
cards.takeaway: Source has grown 7.27% since P58; the latest migration adds 0.33%. Prepared state and reusable annotation add maintenance costs alongside measured compilation gains, so both remain visible.

findings.title: Catch up with upstream and close the observed JavaScript gaps.
paragraphs: The compiler now follows upstream 0592662, incorporating a 95-commit change set. Namespace, Base-library, runtime and native ABI changes were qualified together. The final corrections reuse successful printability visits, handle Min through the existing erasure rules, and replace the separate 64-field call-analysis ceiling with the existing scan budget.

An executable dependency audit retains all 3,174 exact frontend observations against the new reference. Across 1,170 JavaScript-eligible fixtures, fresh Node results plus verified reuse of identical Bun modules and runtime give 1,045 distinct Bend golden passes and zero observed cases where TypeScript passes but Bend fails. The release also passes fresh B2 own-source checking, exact B2/B3 reproduction and installed CLI checks.

stats.label: distinct JS golden passes · Node + Bun

findings.note: The JavaScript total retains 123 unprintable-main exemptions, one shared Process.run failure and one graphics deferral. Native admission still excludes 13 methods. Source grows 94 physical Bend lines (+0.331%); runtime and host costs are counted separately. These finite results do not establish universal conformance or proof validity.

findings.title: Retain program speed while bringing the compiler up to date.
paragraphs: A fresh execution campaign passes all 669 samples across 45 points and 23 sources. Compiled programs average 1.049282× the new TypeScript reference with equal-point weighting; equal-source weighting gives 1.046987×. B1 and B2 emit identical complete programs for the entire measured corpus, so the executed artifacts qualify both producers.

The paired migration comparisons are effectively flat: program execution changes +0.038%, B2 compilation −0.230%, and B1 compilation +0.530%. The new compilation averages are 1.321100× for B2 and 1.402065× for B1. Including imports/API loading gives separate 0.990389× and 0.982634× results. The benchmark reference changed, so P65’s 1.28945× B2 average cannot be read as a direct before/after regression.
flow: Keep reference and clock boundaries visible

stats.label: B2 / B1 compilation time versus new TS

findings.note: The tiny paired changes are descriptive, not established optimizations or regressions. Mandelbrot grid remains 1.619× TS and active raytrace 1.337×; the average does not erase individual gaps. Execution excludes compilation, import, first call and warmup. Both compiler campaigns cover 23 sources and 207 exact-output workers.

findings.title: Make prepared state cheap to read and reuse expensive Base annotations.
paragraphs: Twelve small static readers replace the large cache-decoding loop while retaining eager validation, object shapes and graph sharing. Compiler algorithms stay in Bend; the JavaScript readers handle transport. Separately, Bend produces reusable annotations for sufficiently large Base definitions. Header and identity checks happen before heavy reads, and absent, stale or ineligible products take the ordinary annotation path.

The complete release reduces B2 compilation by 9.03% across all 23 sources, from 1.41737× to 1.28945× the old TypeScript reference. Its import-inclusive average reaches 0.969256×. The isolated first-decode measurement improves from 64.47 to 27.13 ms; a separate same-image artifact ablation reduces Map compilation by 5.13% and map-churn by 3.15%.
findings.note: The isolated decoder and artifact gains are separate experiments and must not be added or multiplied into the release result. Product permission is tied to exact qualified Base content; custom Base keeps the fallback. The release adds 117 physical Bend lines and 146 host-support lines. Several reuse proposals were rejected after unchanged or slower full requests.

sources.title: Selected State10 mechanisms and broad result
Owned annotation products and fallback contract

findings.title: Carry known facts forward and reconstruct prepared data more cheaply.
paragraphs: The compiler retains the Base TODO count and exact checked bound, shares host-signature work, and avoids rendering argument strings that tail-call admission would immediately discard. An indexed cache representation reconstructs the same semantic values with fewer intermediate records. Every record still receives eager structural validation, including unused records.

The complete B2 release cuts compilation time 12.47%, from 1.64387× to 1.43894× TypeScript in its own balanced comparison. All 23 sources improve, with identical emitted programs. In a separate transport experiment, read/hash/validate/materialize time falls from 129.25 to 71.16 ms while serialized size falls only 3.21%: the useful change is cheaper reconstruction, not merely fewer bytes.
flow: Retain exact prefix and type facts
findings.note: A candidate that removed child-type work made the B1 screen 2.34% slower and was removed. Small local gains are not independently established: an identical-image control moved 3.82%. Host support adds 142 lines, and legacy cache-format compatibility remains a maintenance cost. The final B2 result measures the selected bundle.

sources.title: Selected result, mechanisms and rejected work

findings.title: Prepare the world once and lower each definition once.
paragraphs: An authenticated prepared Base world and parser indexes replace repeated reconstruction. A lowering plan owns one immutable annotated context and saves reachable definitions for final emission; already computed arity and host-field facts travel with their consumers. A specialized validated graph decoder makes the retained state economical to load in a fresh process.

The selected B2 takes 20.55% less compilation time across all 23 sources: 2.05505× to 1.63275× TypeScript in the same campaign. Imports plus the first compilation improve 18.18%. Complete emitted modules remain identical. Six adversarial source controls check the context boundary across 45 execution observations, and 558 arity queries agree with the original query, including 74 fallback cases.
flow: Reuse its facts and emitted definitions
findings.note: This is scoped ownership, not a general cache across arbitrary contexts. A generic graph decoder won a warm microbenchmark but lost on fresh requests; only the qualified successor shipped. The release adds 362 physical Bend lines (+1.30%) and 231 host-support lines. No new generated-program speedup is claimed.

sources.title: Final State09 results and ownership contracts

findings.title: Resume checked Base state instead of rebuilding the same work.
paragraphs: The compiler can resume privately authenticated Base freshening and checking state, with source/API binding and conservative fallback. Compact persistent indexes, bounded dependent-term substitution, export-local facts and structured emission transport remove more repeated work. The prepared state restores the checker’s actual fresh-name progress; an early assumption that checking left this state unchanged was disproved and rejected.

The selected B2 release reduces compilation time 45.71%, from 3.816429× to 2.071828× TypeScript. Imports plus the first compilation fall 42.10%, from 2.476542× to 1.433877×. Every source improves in the balanced 23-source, 207-worker campaign, and all full emitted modules match. Fresh own-source checking, exact B2/B3 reproduction and release gates also pass.
flow: Bind prepared state to its producer
Check and compile the new source
findings.note: The broad result combines the selected compiler and host/cache changes; no individual pass owns the full reduction. A binary codec was rejected at 2.26× JSON decode-plus-validation time, and a backend cursor was reverted after mixed B1 results. The release adds 152 host-helper lines; runtime bytes remain unchanged.

sources.title: Final State08 measurements and selected mechanisms
State restoration evidence and retained failures

findings.title: Measure the full corpus and separate startup from compiler work.
paragraphs: The two-program screen expanded to all 23 independent sources behind the 45 runtime points. With the unchanged Phase58 B2, Phase60 found a 2.461× import-inclusive average but 3.794× for compilation alone. Faster Bend startup had hidden part of the compiler-work gap. The survey made equal-source weighting, full output checks and both clocks the basis for later release comparisons.

After Phase61, diagnostics located the remaining excess in prepared-state/loading work and the backend. Actual file reading was only 1.75 ms on average; JSON conversion and validation were much larger. Backend facts were repeatedly rediscovered, but the narrow arity family represented only about 2.3% of CPU sample counts. This directed later experiments toward coherent state and lowering ownership.
flow: Target repeated work with measured budgets

stats.label: P60 B2: imports included / compilation only
P62 diagnostic mean cache file reading

findings.note: Phases59, 60 and 62 changed measurement or analysis tools, not the installed compiler. Diagnostic timings and allocation shares are not additive predicted savings. Repeated requests were still warming, and the B1/B2 generation comparison covered only four sources; it does not replace the 23-source release average.

findings.title: Stop constructing values just to discard them.
paragraphs: Constructor queries now skip unmatched entries without building temporary missing records. Proven numeric residuals reuse their original U32 bits instead of rebuilding Word lists, and structurally known Boolean choices enter the selected branch directly. The constructor probe reduced missing-helper calls from 4,248 to three while preserving its fallback behavior.

Across the complete six-change release, sampled B2 lexer allocation fell from 2,190.55 to 231.95 MB per request. Fresh import-plus-first requests fell from 4.582 to 2.009 seconds for Evening and 2.938 to 1.500 seconds for lexer. The selected B2 takes 2.415× and 2.622× TypeScript time on these two inputs.

stats.label: B2 Evening import + first request · final P58

findings.note: These are combined release results, not isolated attribution. Allocation is a sampled cumulative estimate from one worker per role, not peak RSS. B1 request changes remain small and mixed; B2 later requests are still warming up.

findings.title: Share each recursive dispatcher once.
paragraphs: Exposing more tail calls initially made each entry repeat its recursive component's entire switch. One private dispatcher now serves the component, while each named entry keeps its parameters and a fixed entry state. Per-call state preserves nesting and callback reentry. Reachability also records each target reference only once per definition, retaining encounter order and resource limits.

The final B2/B3 image is 3,821,470 bytes, 1.94% smaller than Phase 56. The complete release emits its own source in 36.058 seconds against a retained 223.475-second Phase 56 run under the same method: a descriptive 6.20× speedup. Both outputs reproduce their own compiler images exactly.
findings.note: The speed ratio compares changed sources and an earlier retained control, not a consecutive pair or dispatch-only effect. The expanded 8.67 MB intermediate was never the starting release. Clean 36.058-second emission is separate from the 39.199-second qualification gate.

sources.title: Final emission timing and retained baseline

findings.title: Measure record syntax in the compiler and its programs.
paragraphs: Ordinary field keys made the compiler faster, but the first combined candidate slowed several generated programs. The selected printer uses quoted prefix keys and keeps the final live field computed; __proto__ always remains computed. This general rule preserves own-property and evaluation-order behavior while balancing the two costs.

The final last01 campaign passes all 45 points and 669 samples. Its equal-point execution ratio is 1.046110× TypeScript, versus a fresh Phase 56 baseline of 1.061731×: 1.47% less time. Evening improves 26.48% and RLE 12.75%. All 19 small regressions remain visible; the largest is 2.949%.

stats.label: execution time · fresh paired P58 campaign

findings.note: The field compromise cost 13–17% against an all-literal compiler diagnostic and missed its approximate 10% target. The final combined release was then measured separately. V8 observations do not establish the precise cause; full release source grows by 314 physical lines.

findings.title: Qualify the compiler that the compiler produces.
paragraphs: Native String.eq now uses JavaScript equality inside its function definition. Existing call sites keep their callback order and partial-application behavior. Alongside removal of seven unused helpers, this small change let the direct B2 image finish both a fresh check of its complete source and emission of an identical successor, B3.

The source check took 29.68 seconds internally. The separate reproduction gate completed in 250.72 seconds, with identical 3,896,951-byte B2 and B3 images. The two compiler generations also emitted identical modules for all 23 benchmark sources and 45 observed points. Phase 58 renews these qualifications for its later image.

stats.label: physical Bend lines · complete P56 change

findings.note: The previous reproduction stopped at 300 seconds, so it supplies no exact speedup. Type acceptance retains the expected unsafe proof-trust refusal and is separate from mathematical proof validity. The installed package remains checked B1.

findings.title: Reuse the type facts the checker already established.
paragraphs: B1 generation of the direct B2 compiler image kept searching the whole book to rediscover a constructor's datatype, even though checked matcher annotations already identified it. Export generation also rescanned recursive argument and result types for Nat conversions. The fixes use the known owner and one complete signature check, with the old paths retained when those facts are unavailable.

On one unchanged compiler source, the second change cut export-wrapper generation from 121.39 to 20.92 seconds. Complete B1 → B2 image generation fell from 198.49 to 96.23 seconds, and the resulting 3,895,592-byte images were exactly equal. These small general changes made the full direct compiler image usable after the earlier deadline failures.

stats.label: fixed-source B1 → B2 image generation · P55
physical Bend lines for both changes

findings.note: Single bounded generation observations with diagnostic overhead, not ordinary request throughput. The original 240-second timeout has no completed baseline time. Eight ordinary-driver observations separately checked the emitted images.

findings.title: Analyze the call graph once.
paragraphs: The direct backend used to store the functions reachable from every function separately. Forward and reverse graph walks now identify recursive groups once and share their facts. This removes repeated closure searches while preserving source order and the existing tail-call decisions.

The production definition budget rose from 512 to 4,096. Using the installed first-stage compiler, five checked source chains through 3,004 declared functions compiled successfully, and every emitted program returned the expected result. All 45 benchmark modules remained byte-identical to Phase 53.

stats.label: declared functions in the largest tested source chain

findings.note: Phase 54 adds 108 physical Bend lines. Graph visits and retained graph data become linear in vertices plus edges, excluding name-index and type-normalization costs. Explicit budgets change the acceptance policy. These are capacity and correctness results, not a measured whole-compiler or program-speed gain.

sources.title: P54 graph algorithm and checked source gates
P54 source accounting and shared ownership

findings.title: Use JavaScript functions and values directly.
paragraphs: Profiles separated expensive public-entry checks from generic call transport. The new backend lowers checked Bend terms to lexical JavaScript functions, native closures and native data. Known calls become ordinary calls, and self or mutual tail recursion becomes loops. This exposes a native-callable interface; applications that need mutable function descriptors keep the explicit legacy backend.

The Phase 52 paired campaign reduced the 45-point geometric execution-time ratio from 2.630605× to 1.123799× TypeScript: a 2.340815× speedup. Distinct emitted JavaScript shrank from 4,194,685 to 1,053,920 bytes, including runtime and observers. Phase 53 subsequently makes this direct interface the default.
findings.note: This changes the JavaScript interface contract. Seven points regressed in P52; closures256 became 2.217× slower while remaining 1.038× TS. Keeping legacy compatibility adds 2,128 physical Bend lines (+9.0%); smaller output does not mean a smaller compiler.

findings.title: Make evaluation order explicit.
paragraphs: The emitter carries statements and a pending value through calls, constructors and lets. It can then inline primitive operations while preserving the reference's observable callback order. Partial applications keep their work deferred, and captured values receive separate held names. A census of four modules found 202 primitive call sites and 30 wrapper declarations removed.

The complete paired campaign moved the 45-point geometric ratio from 1.129266× to 1.069599× TypeScript, a 1.055785× speedup. Original symbolic regression fell from 1.324 to 1.102 milliseconds; ray tracing fell from 57.474 to 48.937 milliseconds. All 669 fresh samples passed their output checks.
findings.note: Twelve of 45 points regressed, at most 3.4%; six timing flags remain. Equal-source weighting gives 1.078× TS. Adds 361 physical Bend lines. Removed syntax is not a measured allocation count or proof of a V8 mechanism.

findings.title: Preserve the bits, and keep the source oracle authoritative.
paragraphs: A cold conversion through an ordinary JavaScript array could lose a NaN payload. Writing directly to fresh typed-array storage preserves the tested bits, with one conversion and no shared mutable buffer. The original fixture's expected result stays 40: the repaired compiler returns 40, where its predecessor returned 39 and pinned TypeScript returned 1.

The original independent source suite advances from 95 to 96 passing scenarios out of 96. All 34 numeric controls, 18 composition controls and two genuine overapplication controls pass their separate contracts. The installed direct default also passes all 66 ordinary and relocated interface checks, including explicit legacy compatibility.
findings.note: These Phase 53 control sets overlap and are not a unique language-test total. Exact reference agreement was 95/96 because TypeScript retained its NaN oracle failure. The later P56/P58 B2 self-reproduction qualification is reported separately.

findings.title: Carry private arrays through the whole computation.
paragraphs: The compiler can keep an Array<U32> as direct backing storage throughout a known private call graph. It checks ownership and effects at the entry, then emits writes as ordered statements. The same representation now reaches recursive tree helpers, so an enclosing private path can benefit too.

In the final paired comparison, original edit distance fell from 10.501 to 5.638 milliseconds, a 1.86× speedup. The 8,192-step fold fell from 172.845 to 109.171 microseconds, reaching 0.956× the TypeScript time. The full 45-point geometric improvement was a smaller 1.057×.

stats.label: faster original edit distance · paired P47

findings.note: Adds 247 Bend lines. The 128-step fold became 1.930× slower (7.603 → 14.671 µs); fresh entry costs matter for short work. Compiler requests rose 0.87–3.75% on three measured inputs.

findings.title: Let a fast representation reach the public result.
paragraphs: An efficient private computation still needs a usable result boundary. Composite-result adaptation let the existing fast region return a complete record containing four arrays. The whole result stays observable. Related changes carry native strings and finite float values through their supported paths.

The complete generic-row case fell from 377.077 to 28.000 microseconds, a 13.467× speedup. That result contributed 72.1% of the net equal-point logarithmic gain. The other 44 points collectively improved 1.023×, while the full corpus improved 1.083×.
findings.note: The gain is concentrated in one case. Adds 406 physical Bend lines; measured Evening and lexer compilation requests rose 3.27% and 4.41%. Tuple-removal experiments that did not improve execution were deferred.

findings.title: Stop scanning the whole book for every declaration.
paragraphs: The checker repeatedly walked preceding definitions to choose fresh binder identifiers. That repeated work grew with each declaration. Computing the bound once removed the scans while keeping declaration visibility unchanged.

On the 16-fill probe, full-book scans fell from 17 to 1. The complete Phase 9 release reduced checking process time from 208.224 to 66.844 seconds. Smaller checking and equality repairs contributed too.

stats.label: checking process time · paired P9 release

findings.note: Mechanism probes explain the change; release timing measures the combined implementation.

findings.title: Keep a value small until someone needs its structure.
paragraphs: Numbers and strings had become large constructor trees. Later passes copied, renamed and serialized those trees repeatedly. Compact literal nodes keep the value small and reveal a constructor view only when a consumer needs it.

A separate same-source census reduced freshened terms from 2,171,045 to 152,620 and constructor/list JSON from 337 MB to 25.3 MB. The final Phase 16 release cut checking time from 30.584 to 12.357 seconds and peak memory by 62.7%.
findings.note: The structural census and final timing use separately identified source snapshots. The release also includes frontend work.

findings.title: One semantic job. One maintained implementation.
paragraphs: The useful simplifications removed competing ways of doing the same work: obsolete algorithms, a second parse to recover source origins, and rechecking a failed body just to format its error. One loader trace and one structured checker result became authoritative.

The dedicated cleanup reduced the compiler from 16,509 to 14,667 physical lines. Later, ordinary definitions and live instances shared one checking traversal, removing 475 lines relative to the immediate predecessor. New conformance and runtime work subsequently grew the codebase.
findings.note: Line counts measure maintained source size. They do not count concepts or prove that every smaller implementation is better.

findings.title: Make direct work visible, and skip proven misses.
paragraphs: A lookup can be expressed as repeated branch closures and trampoline messages—or as a direct tail loop. A small Boolean worker exposed the loop to the existing emitter. The Phase 17 lookup-worker release reduced checking process time by 6.55%.

Later, a scope-index miss proved that a local name was absent, allowing the old scan to be skipped. An index hit still used the original lookup order. That distinction preserves duplicate-name behavior; the Phase 24 release improved checking time by another 4.9% in its own paired window.
findings.note: These are independent release comparisons. Their percentages should not be compounded across changing compiler sources.

findings.title: Carry the right source information forward.
paragraphs: Good error messages need to identify both the right program location and the right semantic checkpoint. A shared renderer restored carets consistently, while source origins attached when terms were created survived later transformations.

Phase 15 closed 144 exact frontend differences. Phase 16 then reduced the remaining differences from 459 to 2 without losing a previous match. Keeping compact literals alongside source information made richer diagnostics affordable.
findings.note: These differences include diagnostics and rejection phase, not only whether a program is accepted.

findings.title: Give the parser the context the language needs.
paragraphs: A context-free parse followed by reconstructed scope could select the wrong error or declaration. One contextual frontend now carries lexical scope, aliases and fresh-name state at the points where they matter. One materializer performs the early or deferred semantic work.

That closed the last two main-suite differences and brought the broader selection from 139 to 196 exact observations. It also removed 300 net lines. The first candidate was 32.8% slower; profiling and lookup repairs recovered that cost, ending 2.9% faster in the final paired comparison. Later releases retained exact agreement on the expanded target.
findings.note: Phase 36 retains 3,026 main and 196 broader exact observations. The selections partly overlap; backend coverage is separate.

findings.title: Make each experiment cheap enough to learn from.
paragraphs: A full self-rebuild took tens of minutes. Routine edits moved to a checked bootstrap plus focused differential cases, with broad suites and fixed-point checks kept as separate integration evidence. Phase 36 reports 42.3 seconds for checked acquisition and 36 focused checks.

The runtime harness separates one-time compilation from execution, validates inputs and outputs, rotates fresh processes and lets experiments select individual cases. Profiles and generated-source comparisons then show where time and allocations go. The Phase 36 one-case symbolic-regression screen took eight seconds.
findings.note: These are workflow observations, not an equivalent-task speedup over a full self-rebuild.

findings.title: Inspect the number directly.
paragraphs: A U32 projection used to allocate 32 linked word nodes, then pass through generic matchers. For eligible checked decision functions, the compiler can instead emit bit tests on the original unsigned number while preserving the ordered decision tree.

On the dense-table diagnostic, execution improved 11.8× and constructor calls dropped from 8,481 to zero per benchmark call. Unsupported result shapes keep the generic path. This established a focused mechanism to pursue in larger programs.
findings.note: A diagnostic kernel result, not a whole-program average. The implementation added 110 Bend lines.

findings.title: Optimize the whole private computation.
paragraphs: Scalar arithmetic and countdowns became ordinary JavaScript expressions and loops. The next step joined them into guarded private regions: direct branches, lexical helpers and reusable tree frames. Keeping these operations together removed costs that were hard to eliminate one tiny call at a time.

Original Mandelbrot execution dropped from 21.379 to 0.212798 milliseconds in the final Phase 30 window: 100.47× faster. Broader tests also led to removing redundant arm prebinding, deleting 64 implementation lines, eight functions and an obsolete module.
findings.note: The gain is workload-specific. Ordinary compiler checking cost 4.86% more, and some small-work canaries regressed.

findings.title: Keep temporary local data inside the computation.
paragraphs: Internal arrays and records were repeatedly crossing generic call boundaries. A checked closed-region boundary let the compiler use direct private workers while keeping public representations, aliases and evaluation order intact.

The original four-pair edit-distance workload fell from 1,900.375 to 70.817 milliseconds. Complete-pair and fold diagnostics also improved in their own window. The boundary gives a precise condition for using the faster representation.
findings.note: Edit-distance compilation request time increased 6.90%; zero-work and generic-row canaries also became slower.

findings.title: Remove wrappers around values used immediately.
paragraphs: Inside the proved region, statement unpacking, typed immediate reads and private field vectors eliminated temporary wrappers. Public boxed records and observable array operations retained their original behavior. The runtime and driver stayed unchanged.

Original edit distance improved again, from 72.266 to 20.398 milliseconds in the Phase 32 window. This focused change added 57 Bend lines. Proposed caches and memoization did not meet the experiment criteria and were left out.
findings.note: This is a separate paired window from Phase 31. Mandelbrot compilation was 1.91% slower.

findings.title: Measure temporary allocations, then remove them.
paragraphs: Profiles pointed to vectors, loop state and tree traversal. Selective inlining replaced immediately consumed fields with loop slots, while closed structural folds walked tagged trees using an explicit postorder stack. Larger proved scalar regions could run directly.

The final comparison measured 6.865× faster symbolic regression and 5.475× faster ray tracing. Separate allocation samples fell by about 8.4× and 9.5× per call on those cases. Broad inlining had caused severe regressions, so the release kept the selective approach.
findings.note: The compiler grew by 979 lines (5.73%) and some compile requests rose 8–34%. Allocation samples are estimates.

findings.title: Pay for the guard once. Compile the producer too.
paragraphs: When the whole call graph is proved pure, covered nested calls can reuse the same guard checks inside a private scope. The scope is restored on exit, and error construction suspends the proof so callback reentry keeps its meaning. Private tree producers and selectors also become direct operations.

Symbolic regression improved from 15.582 to 4.265 milliseconds, and ray tracing from 1,859.589 to 801.893 milliseconds. Seven new control groups cover the tricky boundaries. That Phase 36 release retained exact frontend comparisons and passed all 42 ordinary and relocated CLI checks.
findings.note: Adds 124 lines (0.687%). Compilation medians rose 4.50% / 4.02% for these cases, with overlapping three-sample ranges.
